claims.text: WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args) returns a WebApplicationBuilder, the object an app registers its services and configuration on; registering only records that a service is available, and it is not used until later code asks for it.

claims.text: Calling builder.Build() ends the registration half of Program.cs and produces the WebApplication object; its Run() call, at the end, starts the app listening (on Kestrel).

claims.text: Service registration order does not matter when two calls register different service types, as the last two lines of the Program.cs excerpt (AddScoped<OrderService>, AddSingleton<JwtTokenService>) do; it can matter when two calls register implementations of the same type.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Dependency injection fundamentals (service registration order)

claims.text: app.MapControllers() scans controller classes and registers a method-and-path pair (an endpoint) for each attribute-routed action method; in DonHang.Api/Program.cs it is the only Map* call, so it creates every endpoint this app has.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Routing: Endpoint routing / MapControllers

claims.text: A controller action method's body runs once per matching request, not when app.MapControllers() itself executes at startup.

claims.text: In DonHang.Api/Program.cs, AddControllers() is what lets app.MapControllers() later find and register the project's controller classes; the connection string read there is the text telling the app which database to reach and how to log in.
